text:
maria: Heads-up — we need a clear ruleset for fallback prioritization when a region is down but there are jurisdictional write constraints. We keep patching ad-hoc and ops is getting confused.
ash: +1. Can we codify policy: prefer local-residency-compatible region unless latency impact > X ms?
devon: What's X? 200ms feels high for some latency-sensitive customers. 50-100ms maybe.
li: Also need to account for legal flags (PII residency). If tenant is restricted to EU, fallback outside EU is a no-go even if latency is better.
maria: Right — so policy should be hierarchical: 1) residency permitted 2) latency budget 3) cost tier / capacity.
jules: I worry that strict hierarchy will thrash when capacity is constrained. We need a soft-degrade mode where we can serve reads but queue writes to resident region with a visible degradation.
ash: Agreed. Proposed modes: allow, delay (buffer writes), block. Operators can set mode per-tenant.
li: Can we expose this as a per-tenant config plus a global operator override? Example: tenantX.residency_policy = {allowFallback: false, writeBufferSeconds: 60}
devon: Dev note: buffering writes adds complexity for idempotency and ordering. We need a clear contract: buffered writes are tentative and must be retried with original client idempotency-key.
maria: That's fine. We should also have visibility: when in delay mode, produce a telemetry event: residency.fallback.delay_started with tenant, reason, estimated_delay_seconds.
sre-bot: incident:region-eu1 increased error-rate -> auto-fallback triggered for non-resident tenants at 2026-04-05T10:21:00Z :warning:
ash: Sample policy snippet I sketched — please comment:
```json
{
  "fallback": {
    "priority": ["residency_allowed", "latency_budget_ms", "capacity_score"],
    "latency_budget_ms": 120,
    "write_buffer_seconds": 30,
    "modes": ["allow","delay","block"]
  }
}
```
jules: That looks reasonable. Suggest adding a "consent_check" hook: if consent metadata exists, treat residency_allowed as false unless explicit consent flag is set.
li: +1 for consent_check. Also add an operator override TTL so we don't leave a tenant in override forever.
devon: Operational playbook question: when buffer fills up, do we drop oldest or oldest-per-tenant? We should fail the tenant/route rather than global drop.
maria: Fail-fast per-tenant and send customer-facing status. Ops runbook: 1) detect fallback violation -> 2) mark tenant in "delayed" state -> 3) surface to support -> 4) attempt async replay to resident region.
ash: Can we implement a simple scoring function now? score = residency_ok ? 1000 : 0 + max(0, (latency_budget_ms - measured_ms)) + capacity_score*10. Use that to rank candidate regions.
jules: Keep capacity_score deterministic (0-10). Also cap latency term to [0, latency_budget_ms].
li: Need tests: simulate 3 tenants (EU-only, US-preferred, Global) across failures and verify behavior for allow/delay/block + operator override.
devon: I'll add a small harness in the routing tests. Plan: add policy evaluation module + bench for 50k rps fallback decision performance.
sre-bot: deploybot: canary deploy queued for branch/residency-fallback at 2026-04-05T10:45:00Z :rocket:
maria: Great. Action items: @devon add tests + perf bench, @ash add consent_check hook to policy, @li write ops playbook snippet and TTL override UI, @jules validate scoring math. I'll follow up with an RFC doc after we iterate on the prototype.
ash: One more: we should log chosen_reason (residency/latency/capacity) in every decision for postmortems. Small and cheap but invaluable.
maria: Agreed. End state: deterministic, testable, operator-visible fallback policy that respects jurisdiction first and SLOs second. Thanks all :thumbsup:
